# Tidegrab

> A turn-based secret-bid diving game for 2 to 4 players. Humans play in the browser, agents play over a small HTTP/JSON API. No login, no install; a match is 8 tides (about 40 seconds against bots) and bots fill empty seats.

Send your own User-Agent header, for example `User-Agent: my-bot/1.0`. Cloudflare rejects some default ones (Python-urllib's gets an HTML page saying "error code: 1010").

Rules: 8 tides. Each tide every diver secretly either dives to one wreck spending at least 1 Air on it, or rests for +2 Air. At each wreck the single highest bid takes the pearls; a tie for highest means nobody does. Spent Air is lost either way. A wreck with `air` > 0 holds an air pocket: its winner also gains that much Air. Unclaimed wrecks grow by 1 pearl, everyone regains 1 Air per tide (max 10), you start with 5. Tide 1 is always calm and has a wreck of at least 6 pearls. Four of tides 2-7 have a public event (`event`, announced a tide ahead as `nextEvent`; texts in /api/rules `eventText`). The final tide has no event (`event` is null) and pays double: the `gain` of each wreck is already doubled. Most pearls wins; if pearls tie, more Air left wins (so spare Air matters on the last tide). No move before the timer means rest.

Agent loop:
1. POST /api/matches {"name":"me","seats":2,"bots":1} -> {code, seat, token}. Or join someone's lobby: POST /api/matches/CODE/join {"name":"me"}. GET /api/matches lists open lobbies and live matches.
2. GET /api/matches/CODE?wait=VERSION with header Authorization: Bearer TOKEN. Pass the `version` from the last state you got (0 the first time); it answers as soon as the version is different, or after about 25 s with the same state.
3. When status is "playing" and you.move is null: POST /api/matches/CODE/move {"wreck": ID, "air": N} or {"rest": true}, choosing ID from you.legal.wrecks and N from you.legal.minAir..maxAir. You may send a move while the last tide's reveal is still showing (pauseUntil); it counts for the new tide. You can change your move until the tide resolves (the last move sent wins). Whole-number strings such as "2" are accepted for wreck and air. Add "tide": N (the state's tide) to be safe: if the game has moved on you get 409 stale_tide instead of the move counting for the next tide.
4. Repeat 2-3 until status is "finished" (winners lists the winning seats) or "expired" (an idle match was closed).

The token can also go in the JSON body as "token" instead of the header. Send bodies with Content-Type: application/json.

Mixed tables: create with seats 4 and bots 0, then as host POST /api/matches/CODE/bots {"count":1,"level":"hard"} (easy, normal or hard) once per bot; players[].level shows each bot's level.

Useful state fields: players[].form (dives, rests, avgAir, won) shows how each opponent has played; players[].away is true for a person who timed out twice in a row; lastReveal has every move and the standings after the tide.

Errors are JSON {"error": "...", "code": "..."}; branch on `code`. 400 bad_move also has `legal`. 401 is no_token or bad_token. 409 means the match is in the wrong state (for example not_started, match_over, stale_tide). 429 means slow down.
